The most correct of the views on this in my opinion, and the most like the interpretation of the verse, is the view of those who said: its meaning is: then We returned him to the most abject of ages, to the age of the senile whose minds have gone from old age and decrepitude; so he is in the lowest of the low: in the retreat of life and the departure of the mind. I say that this view is the most correct on this because God, whose mention is lofty, informed of His creation of the son of Adam and His turning him through the states, as an argument thereby against those who deny His power to resurrect after death. Do you not see that He says:
So what causes you to deny, after [this], the Judgement?
; that is, after these proofs. And it is impossible to argue against a people who were denying some matter by something they were denying; the proof against every people is only what

they cannot repel, of what they see with their eyes and perceive, or acknowledge even if they do not perceive it. And since that is so, and the people were deniers of the Fire with which God was threatening them in the Hereafter, while they were witnesses of the people of senility and dotage after youth and vigour—it is known that He argued against them only with what they saw with their own eyes: His turning His creation about, and His transferring them from the state of fine form, youth and vigour to weakness, senility, the exhaustion of life, and the onset of dotage.

x: Others said: Rather, those who believe and do righteous deeds may be included among those who were returned to the lowest of the low, because the most abject of ages may be reached by the believer and the disbeliever. They said: And His saying

They said: its meaning is: then We returned them to the lowest of the low, so their minds went and they became senile, and their deeds ceased, so no good deed is recorded for them after that, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for what they used to do of good in the state of the soundness of their minds and health of their bodies continues for them after their senility and dotage. h
Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds

is a discontinuous exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), because it would be fine to say: Then We returned him to the lowest of the low; but those who believe and do righteous deeds will have a reward uninterrupted, after he is returned to the lowest of the low.
Mention of those who gave the meaning of this view:

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Ibn Abī ʿAdī told us, from Dāwūd, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted
. He said: Any man who was doing righteous work when he was strong and young and then became unable to do it, the reward of that work continues for him until he dies

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted

. He says: when he was acting in obedience to God throughout his youth, then grew old until his mind went, there is recorded for him the like of his righteous work which he used to do in his youth, and he is not held to account for anything he did in his old age and the departure of his mind, because he is a believer and used to obey God in his youth.

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Muʾammal told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm,
m: Then We returned him to the lowest of the low

. He said: to the most abject of ages; and when the believer reaches the most abject of ages, there is recorded for him the like of the best of what he used to do in his youth and health; and that is His saying:
for they will have a reward uninterrupted

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm:
m: Then We returned him to the lowest of the low (5) Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds
: for there is recorded for him of reward the like of what he used to do in health.

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ḥammād b.
m: Abī Sulaymān, from Ibrāhīm, the like of it.

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm:
m: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds
. He said: when he reaches such an old age that he is unable to work, there is recorded for him what he used to do.

x: Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is:
h
Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds
, for their good deeds are recorded for them and their evil deeds are overlooked for them.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Ḥakkām told us, from ʿAmr, from ʿĀṣim, from Abū Razīn, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: Then We returned him to the lowest of the low (5) Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds
. He said: They are those whom old age overtook; they are not taken to task
for any deed they did in their old age while they are senile and do not reason

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayyah told us, from Abū Rajāʾ, he said:
m: ʿIkrimah was asked about His saying:
Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted
. He said: God gives him his full reward, or his [full] work, and does not hold him to account when he is returned to the most abject of ages

c: Yaʿqūb told me, he said: al-Muʿtamir b. Sulaymān told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Ḥakam relate from ʿIkrimah:
Then We returned him to the lowest of the low (5) Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds
. He said: The aged old man; his old age does not harm him, since God has sealed his [life] with the best of what he used to do

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatādah:
m: Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds
. He said: Whoever senility overtakes while he used to do good, will have the like of his reward when

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: then We returned him to the lowest of the low in Hell, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for they will have a reward uninterrupted. According to this interpretation,
h
Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds
are excepted from the pronoun in His saying
h
Then We returned him
; and it was permissible to except them from it since it refers to man, who is in the sense of the plural, as He said:
h
Indeed, mankind is in loss (2) Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds
[al-ʿAṣr: 2, 3].
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Warqāʾ told us,
m: both of them from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
Then We returned him to the lowest of the low (5) Except for those who believe

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, he said:
m: Then We returned him to the lowest of the low
Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds
. Al-Ḥasan said: and it is like His saying:
By time (1) Indeed, mankind is in loss (2) Except for those who believe and do righteous deeds

[al-ʿAṣr: 1–3]. The most correct of the views on this in our opinion is the view of those who said: its meaning is: then We returned him to the most abject of ages, except for those who believe and do righteous deeds in the state of their health and youth, for they will have a reward uninterrupted after their senility, in the same manner as they had for their deeds when they used to work while strong for work. I say that this is the more correct because of what we described of the indication for the soundness of the view that the interpretation of His saying
Then We returned him to the lowest of the low
is: to the most abject of ages. And they differed concerning the interpretation of His saying:
; some of them said: its meaning is: a reward not diminished.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiyah told me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās,
m: for they will have a reward uninterrupted

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning is: not reckoned.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujāhid:
m: for they will have a reward uninterrupted

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid,
Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Muʾammal told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid:
m: for they will have a reward uninterrupted
. He said: not reckoned. He said: Sufyān told us, from Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm:
for they will have a reward uninterrupted

. He said: not reckoned. It has also been said that its meaning is: for they will have a reward uncut. The most correct of the views on this is the view of those who said: for they will have a reward not diminished, as it was for them in the days of their health and youth. And it is in my opinion from their saying: “a ḥabl
manīn,” when it is weak; and from it is the saying of the poet
: “They gave a hundred she-camels (hunaydah), driven by eight [slaves]; in their giving there is no diminishment (mann) nor extravagance (sarāf).” He means that in it there is no shortfall nor error.

x: On the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
So what causes you to deny, after [this], the Judgement? (7) Is not God the most just of judges? (8)
The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His saying:
h
So what causes you to deny after [this]
; some of them said: its meaning is: Who denies you, Muḥammad, after these proofs by which We have argued,
h
about the Judgement (al-dīn)

; he means: about obedience to God and the truth with which He sent you, and that God will resurrect those in the graves. They said: “mā” is in the sense of “man”; because what is meant by it is the son of Adam and those to whom the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent.
Others said: Rather, its meaning is: What causes you, man, to deny the Judgement after these proofs?
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān told us, he said: Sufyān told us, from Manṣūr, he said:
m: So what causes you to deny after [this] the Judgement?
: is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meant by it? He said: “God forbid! Man is meant by it”

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from one
m: So what causes you to deny after [this] the Judgement?
. I said: do you mean by it the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace? He said: “God forbid! Only man is meant by it.”

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from Sufyān, from Manṣūr, from Mujāhid:
m: So what causes you to deny after [this] the Judgement?
: is the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, meant by it? He said: “God forbid! Only man is meant by it.”

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbī:
m: So what causes you to deny after [this] the Judgement?
: it only means man, He saying: I created you in the best of forms, so what causes you to deny, man, after [this], the Judgement

x: Others said: It is only the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who is meant by that, and it was said to him: Be certain, along with the clarification that has come to you from God, that God is the most just of judges.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah,
m: So what causes you to deny after [this] the Judgement?
, that is: be certain, after the clarification that has come to you from God,
Is not God the most just of judges?

. The most correct of the views on this in my opinion is the view of those who said: the meaning of “mā” is the meaning of “man”; and who directed the interpretation of the discourse to: Who denies you, Muḥammad, after what has come to you of this clarification from God,
; that is, about obedience to God and His recompensing the servants for their deeds. And some of the grammarians

have interpreted that in the sense of: What is it that makes you deny that people will be judged by their deeds? As if He said: Who can deny you concerning reward and punishment, after it has become clear to him that We created man as we described? And they differed concerning the meaning of His saying
; some of them said: the reckoning.

x: Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. al-Aswad al-Ṭufāwī told us, he said: Muḥammad b. Rabīʿah told us, from al-Naḍr b.
m: ʿArabī, from ʿIkrimah, on His saying:
So what causes you to deny after [this] the Judgement?

x: Others said: Rather, its meaning
n
is: the judgement of God.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: my father told me, he said: my uncle told me, he said: my father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: So what causes you to deny after [this] the Judgement?
. He says: What makes you deny the judgement of God

. The more correct of the two views on this is the view of those who said: al-dīn in this place is recompense and reckoning. That is because one of the meanings of al-dīn in the speech of the Arabs is recompense and reckoning, and from it is their saying: “As you repay (tadīnu), you will be repaid (tudānu).” And I do not know “judgement (al-ḥukm)” among the meanings of al-dīn in their speech, unless what is meant by it is: What makes you deny, after [this], God's command which He has judged upon you, that you obey Him in it? Then that would be so.

x: And His saying:
h
Is not God the most just of judges?

. The Exalted, whose mention is lofty, says: Is not God, Muḥammad, the wisest of those who judge in His judgements and in the decisive settlement of His decrees between His servants? And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he recited that, according to what has reached us, would say: “Yes.”

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah:
m: Is not God the most just of judges?
: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he recited it would say: “Yes, and to that I am among the witnesses”

c: Abū Kurayb told us, he said: Wakīʿ told us, from his father, from Abū Isḥāq, from Saʿīd b.
m: Jubayr, he said: When Ibn ʿAbbās recited:
Is not God the most just of judges?
, he said: “Glory be to You, O God, and yes”

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, he said:
m: Is not God the most just of judges?
, he said: “Yes, and to that I am among the witnesses.” I think he used to trace that back [to the Prophet]; and when he read
Is not He able to bring the dead to life?
[al-Qiyāmah: 40], he said: “Yes.” And when he recited:
Then in what statement after it will they believe?
[al-Mursalāt: 50], he said: “I believe in God and in what He sent down”

evidence.text: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he recited that, according to what has reached us, would say: “Yes.”

Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatādah: {Is not God the most just of judges?}: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, when he recited it would say: “Yes, and to that I am among the witnesses” (1).
